Retrospective

/reh-truh-SPEK-tiv/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Retrospective means looking back on or dealing with past events and situations.

Retrospective means looking back on or dealing with past events and situations

Worked Example

In a <strong style="color:var(--accent);">retrospective</strong> essay for the paper's final issue, the graduating editor looked back on four years of late-night deadlines and hard-won lessons.

The essay examines events that already happened — four years of the editor's own past — which is precisely what makes it retrospective.

How Retrospective Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

backward-looking

backward-looking: focused on the past

reminiscent

reminiscent: recalling past experiences

reflective

reflective: thoughtfully reviewing what has happened

Antonyms

forward-looking

forward-looking: focused on the future

prospective

prospective: concerned with what is to come

How Strong Is It? — reminiscent → retrospective → elegiac

reminiscent vs. retrospective

reminiscent vs. retrospective: Reminiscent is gentler than retrospective — a reminiscent mood drifts casually through a few memories, while a retrospective review deliberately examines a whole stretch of the past.

elegiac vs. retrospective

elegiac vs. retrospective: Elegiac is more intense than retrospective — an elegiac poem doesn't just look back at what happened, it openly mourns what is gone.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of retrospective.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — retro-

Prefix — retro-: backward (Latin)

Root — spect

Root — spect: to look, to watch (Latin specere/spectare)

Suffix — -ive

Suffix — -ive: tending to; having the quality of

Put it together

Put it together: Retro- ('backward') plus spect ('to look') plus -ive ('tending to') assembles the meaning piece by piece: tending to look backward — examining what lies behind you in time.

Use the root in a new word: introspective

Use the root in a new word: introspective: After the tournament, Dana grew introspective, looking inward to understand why she had frozen during the final match.

Root Check

Word Choice

Formal / analytical

This course teaches retrospective as an adjective ('a retrospective report,' 'a retrospective glance'). You may also meet it as a noun — 'a retrospective' is an exhibit reviewing an artist's whole career. Watch the near-twin retroactive: a retroactive rule reaches back to take effect from a past date, while something retrospective looks back to examine the past. Reviewing versus rule-changing — keep them separate.
